question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = -2x^2 + 10x - 3$ is $x=$
question.explanation:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is given by \[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

We substitute $a = -2$ and $b = 10$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives \begin{align*} \require{cancel} x & = -\dfrac{10}{2(-2)}\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{10}{(-4)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{5}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{5}{2}}.$

question.text: Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola $y=x^2-4x-7.$
question.explanation:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

We substitute $a=1$ and $b=-4$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives \begin{align*} x &= -\dfrac{(-4)}{2(1)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{2}\\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=2.$

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=x^2+4x-11.$
question.explanation:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=1$ and $b=4$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x&=-\dfrac{4}{2(1)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{4}{2}\\[5pt] &=-2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-2.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-2$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= x^2+4x-11 \\[5pt] &= (-2)^2+4(-2)-11 \\[5pt] &= 4-8-11 \\[5pt] &= -15 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-2,-15).$

question.text: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y = x^2 - 6x + 7?$
question.explanation:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is given by \[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a = 1$ and $b = -6$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x & = -\dfrac{(-6)}{2(1)}\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{(-6)}{2}\\[5pt] & = 3. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x = 3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x = 3$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= x^2 - 6x + 7 \\[5pt] &= 3^2 - 6(3) + 7 \\[5pt] &= 9 - 18 + 7 \\[5pt] &= -2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $\big(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2}\big).$

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=3x^2+36x+6.$
question.explanation:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=3$ and $b=36$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x&=-\dfrac{36}{2(3)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{36}{6}\\[5pt] &=-6. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-6.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-6$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= 3x^2+36x+6 \\[5pt] &= 3(-6)^2+36(-6)+6 \\[5pt] &= 108-216+6 \\[5pt] &= -102 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-6,-102).$

The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=-5$ and $b=30$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x&=-\dfrac{30}{2(-5)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{30}{(-10)}\\[5pt] &=3. \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-3,26).$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding an Unknown Coefficient Given the Axis of Symmetry

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=4x^2+kx-2$ is $x=-1.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $-1.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=4$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

\begin{align*} x &= -\dfrac{k}{2(4)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{k}{8}. \end{align*}

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-1,$ so we must have

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{k}{8} &= -1 \\[5pt] -k &= -8 \\[5pt] k &= 8. \end{align*}

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=3$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

question.text: Find the value of $k$ for the parabola $y=kx^2+12x-6,$ shown above.
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since the graph tells us that the axis of symmetry is $x=-3,$ we will set our result equal to $-3.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=12$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

\begin{align} x &= -\dfrac{12}{2(k)} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{12}{2k} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{6}{k}. \end{align}

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-3,$ so we must have

\begin{align} -\dfrac{6}{k} &= -3 \\[3pt] -6 &= -3k\\[5pt] k&=2 . \end{align}
